I haven't brewed anything in over a year but I had been collecting bits and pieces to make a pretty sweet HERMS system, in my opinion.

This is an approximate parts inventory off the top of my head:

  • Two stainless chugger pumps
  • One march pump
  • Many stainless camlock quick disconnects
  • 15 gal Aluminum keggle
  • 15 gal stainless bayou classic boil kettle
  • Copper immersion chiller
  • One blichmann therminator
  • One plate chiller of unknown brand that is bigger than the therminator
  • Some high temp tubing
  • A cooler that was used for batch sparging

I'm sure there are other odds and ends I'm missing but I think those are the important bits.

The tubing I have might be too thin walled and collapses on itself. Tubing suggestions?

Should I use a different type of quick disconnect?

How should I set up sparging?

Is a cooler adequate for a mash tun or should I try something else?

I'm planning on using the keggle as the HLT and pumping the wort through the immersion chiller immersed in the HLT. Good or bad idea?

Anyway, I'm excited about this project and I just want your input.

Thanks!
Getting back into the hobby. Hoping to set up HERMS. Advice?
I can't answer your questions as I'm not familiar with those items, but it sounds like a really nice setup you're working on!

I started down the road to HERMS and never got there, but ended up with a system I like a lot. My inspiration was the Blichmann BrewEasy; basically a two vessel system. I use a cooler as the mash tun and continuously recirculate the mash to the boil kettle and back to the mash tun. I get great clarity and the system doesn't lose hardly any heat. If I need to add any head, I just fire up the burner under the boil kettle. Only needed one pump and one kettle, too. You could always continue on to a full HERMS system, but I'm pretty happy with my two vessel system.

I went 1/2" camlocks and silicon tubing and it works great with the chugger pump.
For any tubing dealing with hot liquid, you should just get silicone tubing.
